# Fazil Digital — factual service and evidence summary

## Business identity
Fazil Digital is a consultant-led SEO and organic growth practice. Visitors work directly with Mohammad Fazil. The current commercial focus is Saudi Arabia: Riyadh first, then Jeddah and Dammam. These are service markets, not verified office addresses. No claim of Saudi registration, certification, client outcome or guaranteed ranking is made.

## Workstreams
SEO consultancy connects research, technical website improvements, useful content, local relevance and measurement. Technical SEO covers crawlability, indexation, site structure, canonical signals and page experience. Local SEO covers genuine eligible business profiles, accurate business details and relevant service information. Content-led organic marketing starts with search intent and original, useful answers. Arabic and English intent require independent research; Arabic content needs qualified editorial localization before publication.

## Working process
Audit the starting point, agree a prioritized strategy, implement with clear responsibilities and measure against a dated baseline. Pricing depends on scope and website conditions; no fixed rate or universal delivery timeline is asserted. SEO review forms prepare a WhatsApp draft. The visitor reviews and sends the message; preparing a draft is not evidence of a delivered or qualified lead.

## Evidence rules
Case-study scope is distinct from measurable results. Publishing an outcome requires source data, baseline and final values, comparison dates, metric definitions, attribution context and permission. No verified quantitative SEO results or Saudi client case studies have been supplied for this phase. Marketing copy and portfolio visuals are not independent proof of outcomes.

## Source and preservation rules
Canonical source URLs use https://www.fazildigital.com/ and trailing slashes for content pages. Sitemap: https://www.fazildigital.com/sitemap.xml
The blog at https://www.fazildigital.com/blog/ includes original Saudi SEO articles and preserves legacy article URLs. Legacy commercial URLs remain accessible and indexable pending evidence review; preservation does not endorse every historical market claim. Canonical HTML articles are preferred citations. Markdown alternatives include noindex and canonical headers.
